trials.name: EVOKE
trials.population: Adults aged 55-85 with mild cognitive impairment or mild dementia of the Alzheimer's type and confirmed amyloid positivity
trials.primary_endpoint: Change in the Clinical Dementia Rating - Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB) score from baseline to week 104
trials.results_summary: Oral semaglutide was not efficacious in slowing clinical progression. Mean changes in CDR-SB score from baseline to week 104 showed no significant difference compared to placebo (treatment difference -0.08, p=0.57). The trial was discontinued due to negative clinical outcome.

trials.name: EVOKE Plus
trials.population: Adults aged 55-85 with mild cognitive impairment or mild dementia due to Alzheimer's disease and confirmed amyloid positivity, including individuals with significant small vessel pathology
trials.primary_endpoint: Change in the Clinical Dementia Rating - Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB) score from baseline to week 104
trials.results_summary: Oral semaglutide failed to demonstrate efficacy in slowing clinical progression. There was no significant difference in CDR-SB score changes compared to placebo (treatment difference 0.10, p=0.46). The trial was discontinued alongside the EVOKE study.

trials.primary_endpoint: Effects of semaglutide on central and peripheral inflammation
trials.results_summary: Registry results have been posted following study completion. This was likely an exploratory or mechanistic sub-study evaluating inflammatory biomarkers, curtailed alongside the broader program.

trials.name: ELAD
trials.population: Mild to moderate Alzheimer's disease syndrome with no diabetes
trials.primary_endpoint: Change in cerebral glucose metabolic rate
trials.results_summary: Liraglutide showed no significant differences in the primary outcome of cerebral glucose metabolism compared to placebo. It also failed to demonstrate significant differences in clinical scales like ADCS-ADL or CDR-SB.

trials.name: GLP1-AD-TTE
trials.population: Target trial emulation using real-world data across five continents
trials.results_summary: Observational target trial emulation designed to explore the discrepancy between real-world evidence showing GLP-1s lower Alzheimer's risk and the negative randomized trials evaluating them as a progression-halting treatment.

related_evidence.description: Primary readout of EVOKE and EVOKE+ phase 3 trials in The Lancet, showing negative clinical outcomes.
Primary readout of the ELAD phase 2b trial of liraglutide in Nature Medicine.

evidence_assessment: The clinical evidence does not support the efficacy of oral semaglutide for the treatment of early Alzheimer's disease. The Phase 3 EVOKE and EVOKE+ trials comprehensively failed to demonstrate any significant clinical benefit over placebo in slowing cognitive decline, as measured by the CDR-SB over 104 weeks. Consequently, Novo Nordisk discontinued the clinical development program for this indication. This lack of efficacy is consistent with the Phase 2b ELAD trial evaluating liraglutide, another GLP-1 receptor agonist, which similarly failed to demonstrate a significant effect on cerebral glucose metabolism or overall clinical dementia rating scales. While observational data suggests GLP-1 receptor agonists may play a role in preventing the onset of Alzheimer's disease, the randomized trial record confirms they are ineffective at halting disease progression once symptoms have manifested.
discrepancies: The document states that the EVOKE trial has no outcomes or data available yet, but peer-reviewed results were actually published in The Lancet in March 2026 demonstrating the trial failed and was discontinued.
The document lists the EVOKE trial enrollment strictly as 1,840 participants based on the registry, while the published manuscript reports 1,855 participants were ultimately randomized in EVOKE.
